title: Compass Only
blurb: No straightedge at all: reflect, invert, and find where lines meet, knowing each line only by two of its points. The Mohr–Mascheroni theorem says a compass is enough for everything.

items.title: Reflect Across a Line
items.text:
There's no straightedge in this lesson: a line is known by two of its points, but it can't be drawn. Construct the reflection of $P$ across the line through $A$ and $B$.

::: Hint
Every point on the line is as far from $P$ as from its reflection.
:::

items.title: Reflect Through a Point
items.text:
Construct the reflection of $P$ through $A$.

::: Hint
The reflection is opposite $P$ on the circle centered at $A$ through $P$.
:::

::: Hint
Six radii step exactly around a circle.
:::

items.title: Inversion
items.text:
Reflection in a circle, or inversion, swaps the inside and outside of $\omega$. Taking $\omega$ as the unit circle, $P$ reflects to the point $P^*$ on ray $OP$ with $OP^* = 1/OP$.

Triangles $OPD$ and $ODP^*$ are isosceles and share the base angle at $O$, so they have the same shape: $OP$ is to $1$ as $1$ is to $OP^*$.

items.title: Reflect in a Circle
items.text:
Construct the reflection of $P$ in $\omega$.

Your construction only needs to work when $P$ is more than half of $\omega$’s radius from $O$.

::: Hint
As in the diagram before this one, find $D$ on $\omega$ as far from $P$ as $O$ is.
:::

::: Hint
There’s no line $OP$ to find $P^*$ on, but $P^*$ is the reflection of $O$ across a chord of $\omega$.
:::

items.title: Midpoint
items.text:
Construct the midpoint of $AB$.

::: Hint
The midpoint is the inverse of a point you can already construct, in a circle you can already draw.
:::

::: Hint
In the circle centered at $A$ through $B$, a point $2 \cdot AB$ from $A$ inverts to the midpoint.
:::

items.title: One Third
items.text:
Construct the point $T$ between $A$ and $B$ with $AT = AB / 3$.

::: Hint
Inversion in the circle centered at $A$ through $B$ turns a point $3 \cdot AB$ from $A$ into one $AB / 3$ from $A$.
:::

items.title: Foot of the Perpendicular
items.text:
Construct the point on the line through $A$ and $B$ that is nearest to $P$.

::: Hint
It’s halfway between $P$ and its reflection.
:::

items.title: Line Meets Circle
items.text:
Construct the two points where the line through $A$ and $B$ crosses $\omega$, which is centered at $O$.

::: Hint
Reflect the whole circle across the line.
:::

::: Hint
A circle is fixed by its center and one of its points.
:::

items.title: Inverting a Line
items.text:
Inversion turns a line that misses $O$ into a circle through $O$: $A$ goes to $A^*$, $B$ to $B^*$, and so on, and the circle turns back into the line.

Reflect $O$ across the line to get $Q$, and the circle’s center is $Q^*$.

items.title: Two Lines Meet
items.text:
Construct the point where the line through $A$ and $B$ crosses the line through $C$ and $D$.

::: Hint
The circles the two lines invert to meet at the center of inversion and at the inverse of the answer.
:::

items.title: Find the Center
items.subtitle: Napoleon’s problem
items.text:
Construct the center of circle $\omega$.

::: Hint
Invert in a circle centered at a point of $\omega$: $\omega$ becomes a line.
:::

::: Hint
That line goes through the two points where the circles cross.
:::

::: Hint
You’ve seen, the other way around, how a circle through the center of inversion relates to the line it comes from.
:::
